_doc: THE DISPATCH-SHAPE KEYSTONE (PLAN §17.1 — the highest-leverage piece). The dispatch analogue of role-registry.json: role-registry owns role IDENTITY (name·home·tier·kind·provider·model·build_chain·claude_pinned); THIS file owns the dispatch SHAPE policy — for each role/skill, the allowed dispatch shapes, the allowed tool ID, the cwd/file-scope/env/secret policy, timeout, budget, output policy, required fixtures+reviewers, and coverage obligations. Every dispatcher (dispatch-claude.js · dispatch-agent.js · future dispatch-skill.js / dispatch-api.js), the N-1 coverage gate, and the drift scanners READ FROM HERE so 'best dispatch shape per unit' is enforceable infrastructure, not doctrine. A role's CLASS is DERIVED from its role-registry attributes via `class_derivation` (single source of identity — no duplicated role list), then merged: defaults <- class <- role_overrides. The three operator-named dispatch failures map directly to contract violations: (i) skipped-gauntlet => a binding_verdict reviewer with no completion record (coverage gate); (ii) API-when-CLI => the `api` shape used by a role whose allowed_shapes lacks it; (iii) in-process-when-subprocess => the `in-process-agent` shape used by a role that forbids it (build-chain). Reader+validator: scripts/dispatch/dispatch-contract.js. Enforcer: scripts/dispatch/dispatch-contract.test.js (planted-violation P5) + scan:dispatch-contract (report-only first, then blocking per PLAN §4).

related.plan: runtime/agent-system-plan/PLAN.md (§17.1 keystone, §North-Star menu, §2 failures, §17.4 coverage record)

shapes._doc: The dispatch-shape menu (PLAN §North-Star). context_cost = the load on Alpha's context. `forbidden_for` names structural prohibitions the validator enforces.

inline.right_when: light work, OR work that needs the LIVE conversation (e.g. session:end handoff)

in-process-agent.right_when: small Claude returns that genuinely need orchestrator context (manager/lead/director consults, β); claude-pinned visual review (MCP/Playwright)
in-process-agent._note: BLOCKED for build-chain (dispatch-guide §2.5) AND for cross-provider reviewers (running a Claude clone silently kills provider diversity — the §2(iii) failure).

subprocess-claude.right_when: build-chain Claude roles; heavy Claude skills (§13)

subprocess-cross-provider.right_when: independent review/security (model diversity; the no-verdict-on-own-work invariant)

api.right_when: ONLY a provider capability with NO CLI (deep-research, GPT-Pro/API-only models)
api._note: PLAN §3/N-2: API availability NEVER implies API dispatch. CLI is mandatory for agent dispatch.

defaults._doc: Applied to every role unless its class or override changes them.

class_derivation._doc: Ordered rules over role-registry attributes. The reader takes the FIRST match. `when` keys are ANDed; a missing key is a wildcard. This keeps the role list single-sourced in role-registry.json — adding a role there auto-classifies it here.

face._doc: alpha/beta/gamma/delta/epsilon — one identity, run as the harness session.

build_chain_worker._doc: frontend/backend/security builders+fixers, stub-scaffold — edit a repo, MUST be isolated.

cross_provider_reviewer._doc: frontend/backend reviewers, qa-reviewer (openai), security-reviewer (gemini) — independent verdict on a different model family.

claude_pinned_reviewer._doc: design-quality, visual-review, test-runner — judgment is VISUAL (Playwright-MCP), so Claude-pinned; independence is the BINDING VERDICT, not provider diversity (a sanctioned carve-out).

manager._doc: directors + leads (incl. quality-lead) — small Claude returns that need orchestrator context; dispatched via the Agent tool, recorded via record-inprocess.

tool_cross_provider._doc: learner — cross-cycle meta-review on a different family (sees the Claude builder/reviewer shared blind spots).

role_overrides._doc: Per-role exceptions merged LAST (defaults <- class <- override). Empty by design — exceptions are a smell; prefer fixing the class derivation. Documented carve-outs only.

epsilon._note: sprint conductor: runs inline as the session AND dispatches the roster via the Agent tool + the ε runtime; its own shape is inline.

skills._doc: SEEDED for skill-execution-routing (PLAN §13) — NOT yet earned. A skill is `inline` until it PASSES §13.6 (runs headless) AND §13.7 (pays + good). `subprocess` entries below are CANDIDATES (classified by weight) carrying subprocess_verified:false until a real smoke run stamps them. The reader treats an unverified `subprocess` skill as `inline` (fail-closed: never trust an unverified subprocess classification). REPORT-ONLY this release.

session:end._note: learn/mine/sleep/TRACKER-reconcile are subprocess-able; the handoff needs the LIVE conversation -> inline-required. Split, don't route wholesale (§13.5).
